summary: At Cana, a nobleman begs Jesus to come and heal his dying son in Capernaum; Jesus sends him home with a word, and the boy recovers at that very hour.
key_insight: The man believed twice. First he “believed the word that Jesus spoke to him” and started home with nothing but a promise. Then, when he learned the hour, “he himself believed, and his whole household.” Trust in a word grew into faith in the One who spoke it.
story: Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where He had made the water wine. A certain nobleman, whose son lay sick at Capernaum, heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee. He went to Him and begged Him to come down and heal his son, for the boy was at the point of death.
Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will by no means believe.” The father pleaded, “Sir, come down before my child dies!”
Jesus said to him, “Go your way; your son lives.” The man believed the word Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.

As he was going down, his servants met him with the news: “Your son lives!” He asked them the hour when the boy began to get better. They said, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.” The father knew it was the very hour when Jesus had said to him, “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, and his whole household.
This was the second sign Jesus did after He had come out of Judea into Galilee.

scene.label: A royal official
scene.text: The word translated “nobleman” means a man in the king’s service. He probably served Herod Antipas, whom people called king though Rome made him only a tetrarch (Mark 6:14). He is a different man from the Gentile centurion of Capernaum whose servant Jesus healed later (Matthew 8:5–13).

scene.label: Down to Capernaum
scene.text: From Cana in the hills to Capernaum on the lakeshore was a steep descent and a long day’s walk, perhaps sixteen to twenty miles. That is why John keeps saying “come down” and “going down.”

scene.label: The seventh hour
scene.text: Counting from sunrise, the seventh hour was about one in the afternoon. The servants called it “yesterday” when they met the father on the road. Since a Jewish day began at sunset, they may have met that same evening, or the father may have stopped for the night on the way home.

scene.label: Signs
scene.text: John calls Jesus’ miracles signs: works that point beyond themselves to who He is. He numbers the first two, both at Cana (John 2:11; 4:54), and he writes so that readers “may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God” (John 20:31).

witnesses.john: John alone tells this sign, and he ties it to the first: both happen at Cana, and both are numbered. Coming right after the Samaritans believed “because of His own word” (John 4:41), it shows a Galilean father learning the same lesson: to trust Jesus’ word before he sees.

seeing.reveals: Jesus does not need to be in the room. His word, spoken in Cana, reached a sickbed in Capernaum at the very hour He spoke it.
seeing.living: The father wanted Jesus to come with him; Jesus gave him a promise instead and sent him home on it. Faith often looks like that long road, holding a word from Jesus before you can see the result.
seeing.ponder: What word from Jesus are you being asked to walk home on before you see it fulfilled?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus asks us to trust His word before we see His work.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus’ rebuke in verse 48 is plural, “you people,” aimed at Galileans who wanted signs. The father does not argue; he simply asks again. Jesus sends him away with nothing to see, only a word, and the man believes it.
